target: लिफ़्ट बंद है, हम सीढ़ियों से ऊपर गए।
english: The lift is out of order, we went up by the stairs.
reason: Unnatural word order — "विकलांग रैंप से व्हीलचेयर पर चढ़ा" literally reads "the disabled man climbed onto a wheelchair off the ramp", which is not what the English says; विकलांग is also a dated label. Replacement keeps the same instrumental से + motion-verb pattern in an everyday situation.

target: पार्टी में सबको खाना परोसा गया।
english: Everyone was served food at the party.
reason: Niche ritual trivia in the passive — "a coconut was broken at the housewarming" is cultural knowledge, not a sentence a learner will ever produce. Replacement keeps the same में + passive (…या गया) frame with everyday content.

target: हमने मेहमानों को कमरे में बिठाया।
english: We seated the guests in the room.
reason: दालान is dated/regional (few urban speakers use it), and the subjectless clause reads like a caption. Replacement keeps the same को + बिठाया pattern with an ordinary word and an explicit ने-subject.

target: चाबी से दरवाज़ा खोलकर हम अंदर गए।
english: We opened the door with the key and went inside.
reason: Niche tool vocabulary (कुदाल) plus a subjectless, translationese clause — no one narrates digging a pit with a spade. Replacement keeps the identical से + …कर conjunctive-participle structure with everyday vocabulary.

target: आंटी जी, अंदर आइए और बैठिए।
english: Auntie, please come inside and sit down.
reason: "बहू जी" as a form of address is odd — one does not use आइए/बैठिए honorifics to one's own daughter-in-law, and a learner will never address anyone this way. Replacement keeps the same vocative + two आइए-imperatives with a form of address people actually use.

target: बच्चों ने हाथ धोकर खाना खाया।
english: The children washed their hands and then ate.
reason: Pointless niche content — soldiers marching in step in a parade is not language a learner needs. Replacement keeps the same ने-perfective + …कर participle chain in a daily-life situation.

target: चम्मच से दही अच्छी तरह मिला लो।
english: Mix the yogurt well with a spoon.
reason: "दही सजाओ" is unnatural — सजाना means to decorate, and nobody says it of yogurt; you डालो or मिलाओ. Replacement keeps the instrumental से + familiar imperative in a real kitchen instruction.

target: कुकर में दाल धीमी आँच पर पकाओ।
english: Cook the lentils on a low flame in the cooker.
reason: Decorative cookware detail (copper handi) that no learner will use or hear. Replacement keeps the exact में + पर + imperative frame with the pot people actually cook dal in.

target: हम कल शाम मिलेंगे, यानी छह बजे के बाद।
english: We'll meet tomorrow evening, that is, after six.
reason: Textbook motto — "her hard work paid off" is a proverb-style moral, not speech. Replacement keeps the same यानी clarifying-clause pattern in an ordinary exchange.

target: रोज़ सुबह टहलना मेरी आदत है।
english: Walking every morning is my habit.
reason: Preachy cultural motto ("welcoming guests is an Indian tradition") — reads like a civics poster. Replacement keeps the same infinitive-as-subject + है structure with a sentence a person would really say.

target: होटल वाले ने हमें ऊपर वाला कमरा दिया।
english: The hotel guy gave us the room upstairs.
reason: Stilted translationese — "होटल मालिक ने मुसाफ़िरों को ठहराया" is written-report register; in speech you say होटल वाले ने कमरा दिया. Replacement keeps the ने + को/indirect-object perfective pattern in usable travel Hindi.

target: स्कूल के कार्यक्रम में बच्चों को इनाम दिए गए।
english: Prizes were given to the children at the school event.
reason: Officialese — "पुरस्कार वितरण समारोह" is bureaucratic ceremony language rather than everyday speech. Replacement keeps the same में + को + plural passive (दिए गए) in an ordinary register.
